task: Fix the findings from an external pre-publish review of the elenwatch npm package (an in-process LLM provider HTTP traffic interceptor) so that 0.2.1 becomes publishable: blocker 1 — a streamed fetch request body over maxBodyBytes is truncated on the wire (data corruption); blocker 2 — the ESM build does not work at all (extensionless emitted specifiers + bare require() under ESM + extensionless .d.ts, and the postbuild verifier never actually loads the ESM entry); plus five should-fix items (lint error, unconditional cap-trip console.error, missing prepublishOnly, 31-line package README, undocumented aggressive redaction needles). User decisions: fix ESM properly (not CJS-only); full README sections; CI + CHANGELOG deferred to horizon 3.

analysis.objective: Resolve the two blocker findings (streamed-body data corruption; broken ESM build) and the five should-fix findings from the external pre-publish review so that elenwatch 0.2.1 becomes a publishable npm package, using the review's 'Fix:' prescriptions as authoritative.
analysis.successDefinition: In packages/elenwatch: (1) a streamed fetch request body larger than maxBodyBytes is delivered to the wire in full and byte-identical while only the capture-side buffer is truncated, proven by a test sending a 5000-byte streamed body with a 1024-byte cap; (2) import('elenwatch') against the packed tarball succeeds under Node ESM with undici fetch-capture and the OTEL logger functional in an ESM consumer, and dist/esm/*.d.ts typecheck cleanly under moduleResolution nodenext; (3) a pack-and-import smoke test (npm pack + install into a temp dir + node --input-type=module import + CJS require) runs under npm test and would fail on any of the ESM regressions above; (4) npm run lint exits 0; (5) the cap-trip console.error is suppressed when onBodyDropped is provided; (6) package.json has a prepublishOnly running build + test; (7) the package README has full Installation / Configuration / Limitations / API sections covering capturePayloads default false, redaction's case-insensitive substring needles, maxBodyBytes/onBodyDropped, the undici optional-peer requirement, requestTransform being http-path-only, the streamed-request-body buffering caveat, and the one-interceptor-per-process model; (8) npm test and npm run build pass green with new regression tests for blockers 1 and 2.
assumptions: The repo's real gates are npm run build, npm run lint, and npm test (jest 29 + ts-jest, not vitest); a phase counts as done only when these are green.

Writing .js extensions on relative import specifiers in source .ts files would break ts-jest resolution (no moduleNameMapper, moduleResolution node), so the ESM fix rewrites the emitted dist/esm output in postbuild.mjs rather than editing source.

createRequire replaces the bare require(...) for undici and @opentelemetry/api; because import.meta is invalid under tsconfig.cjs.json, a build-tolerant mechanism (ESM-only shim, .cts/.mts split, or bare-require retained only for the CJS emit) is chosen at execution, with the pack-and-import smoke test as the acceptance check.

The public API surface (Interceptor class, .install()/.restore(), Logger, InterceptorOptions, onBodyDropped, VERSION) stays stable; these are packaging/correctness fixes shipping as 0.2.1 without a version bump.
The streamed-request-body branch keeps its capture-before-dispatch buffering behavior; only a README caveat is required, not a rewrite to true streaming.
README canonical wording is mirrored from src/options.ts docstrings and the real exports in src/index.ts.
The pack-and-import smoke test runs in the existing jest tooling (temp dir + child process) and skips cleanly when npm is unavailable.
risks: Adding .js extensions in source could regress the CJS build or ts-jest resolution — mitigated by doing the rewrite in postbuild against emitted dist/esm only.
createRequire-based lazy loading may change the timing or failure mode of the undici/otel try/catch, altering the horizon-1 'peer absent -> skip' behavior that tests depend on.
import.meta.url does not compile under tsconfig.cjs.json (module: commonjs); a naive createRequire(import.meta.url) in source fails the CJS build.

The separate-arrays fix for blocker 1 must preserve the horizon-1 streamed-request-body race fix (capture awaited before dispatch) and the drain-error propagation path, or it reintroduces a fixed bug.
A naive smoke test that installs from the workspace rather than the packed tarball would pass while the real published artifact stays broken.
dist/esm .d.ts extension rewriting can desync from the .js rewriting, leaving one tree still failing nodenext consumers.
console.error gating logic could suppress the operator signal in cases where onBodyDropped is set but throws, leaving operators with no visibility.

analysis.domainShapeReason: The task is entirely library-internals plumbing — HTTP interceptor buffer handling, dual-format module resolution, lazy native-require loading, lint and package metadata, and user-facing docs — with no business entities, rules, or workflows.

ubiquitousLanguage.meaning: The undici Dispatcher subclass whose dispatch() intercepts global fetch traffic; host of the streamed-request-body branch.
Two now-distinct byte arrays: the capture buffer is truncated at maxBodyBytes for logging; the wire body is the untruncated bytes actually sent to the upstream server.
The helper that accumulates body chunks and, given a byte-cap context, stops appending and flips bodyDropped once a direction's byte counter would exceed the cap.
The configurable per-direction capture byte bound and the structured callback fired (with BodyDroppedInfo) when it trips.
dist/cjs and dist/esm trees emitted by tsconfig.cjs.json and tsconfig.esm.json, with postbuild.mjs writing per-tree package.json type markers.
A relative import like from './interceptor' that Node's ESM resolver rejects; must carry a .js extension in both emitted .js and .d.ts files.
Loading optional native peers (undici, @opentelemetry/api) via createRequire so resolution works in both CJS and ESM instead of a bare require() that throws 'require is not defined' under ESM.
A verifier that runs npm pack, installs the tarball into a temp dir, and loads elenwatch as both an ESM module and a CJS module to prove the published artifact actually loads.
elenwatch patches http.ClientRequest.prototype and the global undici dispatcher process-wide, so only one Interceptor can be active per process.

discoveryFindings.finding: The AsyncIterable/ReadableStream branch of dispatch() (src/interceptor.ts ~398-441) drains chunks into a local `chunks: Buffer[]`, feeds each chunk to appendChunk(chunks, chunk, undefined, reqCapCtx), pushes them into state.requestBodyChunks, sets capturedEnd/finished, then does options.body = Buffer.concat(chunks) and this.original.dispatch(...). The drain-error path (~428-438) finalizes capture then calls handler.onError?.(e) and syntheticReq.emit('error', e).
discoveryFindings.implication: The wire body reuses the same cap-gated `chunks` array, so on cap trip both capture AND wire truncate. Fix: a separate ungated wire array; preserve the horizon-1 capture-before-dispatch ordering and the drain-error path.

discoveryFindings.area: appendChunk and the single console.error site
discoveryFindings.finding: appendChunk (src/interceptor.ts ~560-636) is a module-level free function taking an inline anonymous cap-context type {state, direction, cap, onDropped}. On nextBytes > cap it sets bodyDropped[direction], clamps bytesCaptured, builds BodyDroppedInfo, calls console.error at line 623 (the only console.error in the file), then onDropped?.(info) in try/catch, then returns without pushing.
discoveryFindings.implication: A separate ungated wire array (not appendChunk's return) is needed for blocker 1. Gating the single console.error at line 623 on capCtx.onDropped === undefined covers both request and response directions.

discoveryFindings.area: Lazy require of optional peers under ESM
discoveryFindings.finding: src/interceptor.ts:87-98 and src/otel.ts:36-44 both do try { x = require('...') } catch { x = undefined }, each with an eslint-disable for no-require-imports. undici and @opentelemetry/api are optional peers AND devDependencies (present in the workspace).
discoveryFindings.implication: Bare require() throws 'require is not defined' under ESM and the catch swallows it, so ESM consumers silently lose all fetch capture and the OTEL logger even when the peers are installed. Switch both to createRequire; import.meta.url is invalid under tsconfig.cjs.json so a build-tolerant mechanism is required.

discoveryFindings.finding: tsconfig.esm.json uses module esnext / moduleResolution bundler -> dist/esm with extensionless relative specifiers in both .js and .d.ts. tsconfig.cjs.json uses module commonjs / moduleResolution node -> dist/cjs with require('./x'). dist/esm is flat (no subdirectories). No prepublishOnly script. exports['.'].types is already split per import/require condition (horizon 1).
discoveryFindings.implication: Node's ESM runtime loader and a nodenext typecheck both reject the extensionless dist/esm specifiers. Rewrite emitted dist/esm .js + .d.ts in postbuild; leave dist/cjs and source untouched.

discoveryFindings.finding: scripts/postbuild.mjs writes per-tree package.json type markers then checkTree(dist/esm): for each file named index.*.js it asserts a line starting with import/export exists; every other file is unchecked; it recurses into subdirectories.
discoveryFindings.implication: The 'ESM tree verified as modules' claim is a regex on index.js only. postbuild.mjs is where the specifier-rewrite step and a hardened verifier (fail the build on any remaining extensionless relative specifier) belong.

discoveryFindings.finding: package.json jest block: moduleFileExtensions [js,json,ts], testRegex (/__tests__/.*|(\.|/)(test|spec))\.ts$, ts-jest transform with tsconfig.json, no moduleNameMapper.
discoveryFindings.implication: Adding .js extensions to source relative imports would break ts-jest resolution — the postbuild dist-rewrite avoids source. A new *.smoke.test.ts / *.test.ts file is auto-collected by npm test and runs transitively under prepublishOnly.

discoveryFindings.finding: In the 'AsyncIterable body that throws mid-stream' test, `let rejectedWith: unknown = undefined;` is assigned in the catch but never read; the only assertion is expect(rejected).toBe(true).
discoveryFindings.implication: Trivial one-line-pair deletion; it is the single remaining lint error carried through all of horizon 1, so removing it makes npm run lint exit 0.

discoveryFindings.finding: packages/elenwatch/README.md is 31 lines (# elenwatch / ## Install / ## Usage), documenting only the logger: option and new Interceptor(...).install()/.restore(). options.ts: capturePayloads default false; redaction masks ~70 built-in field-name needles matched as case-insensitive substrings (redaction.ts DEFAULT_SENSITIVE_FIELDS); maxBodyBytes default 10 MiB, per-direction; BodyDroppedInfo = {host, direction, bytes, cap}; the requestTransform docstring overclaims — it is only wired on the http write/end path, never in WrappingDispatcher.dispatch; responseTransform currently has zero invocation sites. index.ts exports the Interceptor class, Logger type, otelSpanLogger, VERSION, etc. (no free install/restore).
discoveryFindings.implication: The README API section must document the Interceptor class, Configuration must state redaction is case-insensitive substring matching with an over-redaction warning, and Limitations must state requestTransform is http-path-only (fetch request bodies captured but never transformed).

discoveryFindings.finding: startServer(handler?) at interceptor.test.ts:40-72 returns {server, port, close}. Fetch suites use udPeer = require('undici') in try/catch and itIfUd = udPeer ? test : test.skip, calling fetch(url, {method:'POST', headers, body, duplex:'half'}). The horizon-1 race test builds a 3-chunk ReadableStream with await Promise.resolve() between pulls. packaging-build.test.ts relies on the pretest build and runs execFileSync('npm', ['pack', '--dry-run', ...]) then parses the listing.
discoveryFindings.implication: The new smoke test follows packaging-build.test.ts (real npm pack + install into mkdtemp + two node children). The new streamed-body regression test follows the itIfUd + startServer + ReadableStream pattern with a server-side full-body assertion.

phases.name: Split wire body from the capture buffer
phases.goal: In WrappingDispatcher's streamed-request-body branch, accumulate the bytes sent upstream in an array separate from the size-capped capture buffer, so a request body larger than maxBodyBytes reaches the server byte-identical while only the logged copy truncates.
phases.rationale: This library intercepts outgoing HTTP request bodies so it can log them. When a caller streams a request body, the current code drains it into a single array that stops growing once a configurable size limit (maxBodyBytes) is reached, then hands that same truncated array to the real server, corrupting the actual request. The bytes kept for logging and the bytes put on the wire must be tracked independently. WrappingDispatcher is the undici Dispatcher subclass that intercepts global fetch traffic.
changes: In the Symbol.asyncIterator branch of the drain IIFE (interceptor.ts around lines 414-427), introduce a full untruncated wireChunks: Buffer[] that every iterated chunk is pushed to unconditionally, with no cap check on that push path.
Keep feeding the capture side through appendChunk(..., reqCapCtx) so only the capture buffer (state.requestBodyChunks) truncates at the cap and still flips bodyDropped / fires onBodyDropped.
Set options.body = Buffer.concat(wireChunks) - never the capped capture array - immediately before this.original.dispatch(options, wrappedHandler).

Preserve the horizon-1 capture-before-dispatch ordering (drain fully, set capturedEnd/finished, then dispatch in the same async frame with no timer or microtask hop) and the drain-error path (catch -> finalize capture -> handler.onError?.(e) -> syntheticReq.emit('error', e)).

Add a regression test: stream a 5000-byte request body with maxBodyBytes: 1024 to a local HTTP server; assert the server received all 5000 bytes byte-identical and the captured/logged body is <= 1024 bytes; include a non-cap-multiple and/or binary payload case.
While editing interceptor.test.ts, delete the unused rejectedWith variable near line 1846 that currently fails npm run lint.
inputs: src/interceptor.ts asyncIterator drain branch (~lines 397-440)
appendChunk cap-context behavior (~lines 560-635)
horizon-1 capture-before-dispatch race fix and drain-error path (must be preserved)
review 'Fix:' prescription for blocker 1 (separate wire/capture arrays)
phases.expectedResult: A passing regression test proving a 5000-byte streamed request body is delivered to the server in full and byte-identical while the captured body is <= 1024 bytes under maxBodyBytes=1024, and npm run lint exits 0.
phases.compensation: Revert the interceptor.ts diff; the extra wire array is additive and holds no persisted state.

rubric.label: Wire body byte-identical to source even when cap trips
rubric.ruleStatement: In the streamed-request-body (Symbol.asyncIterator) branch, the bytes dispatched to the real server MUST equal the full concatenation of every iterated chunk, regardless of maxBodyBytes, and MUST come from an accumulator distinct from the size-capped capture buffer. 10 = a separate accumulator plus a test proving byte-identity on a non-ASCII and non-cap-multiple payload; 8 = separate accumulator and a 5000-byte length+content check; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: The asyncIterator drain branch declares a separate full accumulator (e.g. wireChunks: Buffer[]) every iterated chunk is pushed to unconditionally, with no cap check on that push path.

options.body is reassigned to Buffer.concat(wireChunks) (or equivalent full buffer) before this.original.dispatch(options, wrappedHandler), and is never assigned from state.requestBodyChunks / the capture array.
The phase's regression test streams a 5000-byte body with maxBodyBytes: 1024 to a local HTTP server; the server-side received byte length is exactly 5000 and the bytes match the source.
A second assertion confirms the captured/logged body is <= 1024 bytes.
A non-cap-multiple case (e.g. 2049 bytes with cap 1024) OR a binary (non-UTF8) payload confirms the server still receives an identical byte sequence.
failureExamples: Plausible: dev calls Buffer.concat over an array that shares references with the capture path, so a later capture-side trim mutates the wire buffer too.
Plausible: the wire accumulator decodes each chunk to a string and re-encodes at dispatch, corrupting multibyte or binary payloads even though total length looks right for ASCII test data.
The test only asserts res.statusCode === 200, never comparing received body length or content.

rubric.label: Capture buffer still truncates and fires onBodyDropped
rubric.ruleStatement: The capture side MUST continue to flow through appendChunk(..., reqCapCtx) so only state.requestBodyChunks truncates at the cap, bodyDropped flips exactly once, and onBodyDropped fires with the correct BodyDroppedInfo. 10 = per-chunk appendChunk retained and both over-cap and under-cap paths asserted; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: Each iterated chunk is still passed to appendChunk with the request cap context; the split did not bypass or duplicate that call.
With maxBodyBytes: 1024 and an onBodyDropped spy on a 5000-byte streamed body: the callback is invoked once with request-direction info consistent with options.ts.
With a streamed body smaller than the cap: onBodyDropped is NOT called and bodyDropped stays false.
Captured request body for the over-cap case is <= maxBodyBytes; for the under-cap case it is the exact full bytes.
Pre-existing appendChunk / cap-context unit tests pass unchanged.
failureExamples: Plausible: dev feeds appendChunk the already-joined full buffer once instead of per-chunk, so the per-chunk byte counter overshoots and onBodyDropped reports the wrong count.
Plausible: bodyDropped is derived from wireChunks.length > cap, so it never flips because wireChunks is uncapped.
Callback fires once per chunk after the cap is exceeded instead of exactly once.

rubric.label: Horizon-1 capture-before-dispatch ordering intact
rubric.ruleStatement: The branch MUST still fully drain the async iterator, set capturedEnd/finished, and then dispatch within the same async frame - no added timer, setImmediate, process.nextTick, or unnecessary await hop between finalizing capture and calling this.original.dispatch. 10 = git diff shows only the wire-array insertion with ordering untouched; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: After the drain loop, capture finalization happens before this.original.dispatch with no scheduling primitive introduced between them.
git diff against the horizon-1 code shows the ordering statements reordered only to insert the wire accumulator, not to defer dispatch.
The horizon-1 race-condition regression test still passes unchanged.
No new async wrapper or Promise chain pushes dispatch to a later microtask tick relative to capture finalization.
failureExamples: Plausible: dev wraps the concat in await Promise.resolve(...) or an awaited async helper, inserting a microtask hop that reopens the horizon-1 race.
Plausible: wireChunks is concatenated inside a .then() off the drain promise, moving dispatch out of the drain's async frame.
Dispatch is moved above capture finalization.

rubric.label: Drain-error propagation path preserved
rubric.ruleStatement: If iterating the request body throws, the catch MUST still finalize the capture, then call handler.onError?.(e) and syntheticReq.emit('error', e) - the wire-body split must not swallow, reorder, double-fire, or dispatch a partial body. 10 = a test asserts the server received no request on a mid-stream throw; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: The catch block still contains, in order: capture finalization, handler.onError?.(e), syntheticReq.emit('error', e).
this.original.dispatch is NOT called when the drain throws (a partial wireChunks buffer is never dispatched).

A test with an async-iterable request body whose iterator throws mid-stream: the fetch/request rejects or emits 'error' with that error, capture is finalized, and the server receives no request (or the test asserts dispatch was not invoked).
The error is propagated once, not twice.
failureExamples: Plausible: dev moves options.body = Buffer.concat(wireChunks) and this.original.dispatch into a finally or after the try/catch, so a drain error now also dispatches a truncated body.
Plausible: Buffer.concat throws inside the drain catch on mixed string/Buffer entries, misreporting an internal bug as a request-body error.
Catch reordered so emit('error') precedes capture finalization.

rubric.label: Lint passes and the diff stays scoped
rubric.ruleStatement: npm run lint MUST exit 0 (including removal of the unused rejectedWith variable near interceptor.test.ts:1846), and the change MUST be confined to the streamed-request-body branch plus its tests. 10 = the dead variable is deleted (not underscore-prefixed or disabled) and git diff --stat touches only interceptor.ts and interceptor.test.ts; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: npm run lint in packages/elenwatch exits 0.
The unused rejectedWith variable near line 1846 of interceptor.test.ts is deleted (grep confirms it is gone) and its removal breaks no assertion.
npm test (or the interceptor suite) exits 0 with the new regression test present and passing.
git diff --stat touches only interceptor.ts and interceptor.test.ts; the buffered/known-length request-body branch and the response path are unchanged.
No change to public exports, options.ts, or the CJS/ESM build config.
failureExamples: Plausible: dev prefixes _rejectedWith or adds an eslint-disable instead of deleting the dead variable.
Plausible: the new regression test leaves a local HTTP server listening (no server.close() in a finally/afterEach), so the suite hangs or flakes in CI.
The refactor also rewrites the buffered request-body branch 'for consistency'.

phases.healerHint: If a correctness property is untested, add a dimension asserting the dispatched wire body is byte-for-byte identical to the concatenated source under a tripped cap (distinct accumulator, non-ASCII and non-cap-multiple payloads), and verify the horizon-1 same-async-frame ordering and the catch -> finalize -> onError -> emit('error') drain-error path survive the split unchanged.

phases.name: Replace bare require with createRequire for optional peers
phases.goal: Load the optional undici and @opentelemetry/api peers via a createRequire-built require so fetch capture and the OpenTelemetry logger work when elenwatch is consumed as an ES module instead of being silently swallowed by the surrounding try/catch.
phases.rationale: The library lazily loads two optional dependencies with a bare require(...) call wrapped in try/catch. In a native ES module there is no require in scope, so the call throws, the catch treats it as 'peer not installed', and both features do nothing even when the peer is actually present. createRequire from node:module builds a working require. Because import.meta is invalid in the CommonJS build output, the exact mechanism must be one that compiles and runs under both emitted formats.
changes: Replace the bare require('undici') at interceptor.ts:87-98 and require('@opentelemetry/api') at otel.ts:36-44 with a require obtained from createRequire (node:module).

Because import.meta.url does not compile under tsconfig.cjs.json (module: commonjs), pick a build-tolerant mechanism: a dedicated ESM-only shim module the ESM build resolves, a .cts/.mts split, or keeping the bare require for the CJS emit while the ESM emit gets createRequire; verify with tsc -p tsconfig.cjs.json --noEmit AND tsc -p tsconfig.esm.json --noEmit.
Narrow the catch so only module-not-found (MODULE_NOT_FOUND / ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND) is treated as 'peer absent'; a genuine load error is not swallowed.
Keep the peer-absent behavior: the handle stays undefined and install()/restore()/otelSpanLogger stay inert; the horizon-1 'peer absent -> skip' tests pass unchanged.
Remove or retarget any now-unused eslint-disable directive for no-require-imports so npm run lint (with --report-unused-disable-directives) stays green.
inputs: interceptor.ts lazy-require block (~lines 87-98)
otel.ts lazy-require block (~lines 36-44)

rubric.ruleStatement: The lazy loader for undici and @opentelemetry/api must build its require via createRequire from node:module in a form that compiles and runs under both tsconfig.cjs.json and tsconfig.esm.json. 10 = both tsc projects and both built entrypoints load the peer with no import.meta in dist/cjs; 8 = both tsc projects pass and the ESM entry loads the peer; minScore = acceptable.

rubric.label: Present peer actually loads under ESM

The catch does not treat a genuine module-resolution success as failure.

No new console.warn/console.error on the peer-absent path.
createRequire is constructed once (module scope or memoized), not rebuilt on every install() call - or a comment explains why per-call.
failureExamples: The catch now logs console.warn('optional peer failed to load', err) on every ESM run without the peer, breaking a test asserting clean output.
createRequire(import.meta.url) is at module top level in otel.ts, which is also imported by a CJS-only test path, throwing at import time before any catch can run.

phases.healerHint: Keep import.meta out of any file tsconfig.cjs.json compiles (use an ESM-only shim, a .cts/.mts split, or a runtime typeof-require guard), apply the identical change to both interceptor.ts and otel.ts, narrow the catch to module-not-found codes so real errors are not swallowed, verify with tsc -p tsconfig.cjs.json --noEmit AND tsc -p tsconfig.esm.json --noEmit plus a load of both built entrypoints, and drop any now-unused eslint-disable.

phases.name: Add .js extensions to emitted ESM import specifiers
phases.goal: Extend scripts/postbuild.mjs to append .js to every relative import/export specifier in the emitted dist/esm .js and .d.ts files, harden its verifier to fail the build if any extensionless relative specifier remains, and add a prepublishOnly script - so Node's ESM loader and a nodenext typecheck accept the published ESM tree and a stale build cannot be published.
phases.rationale: TypeScript emits relative imports with no file extension (from './interceptor'). Node's ES module loader and strict nodenext type resolution both reject extensionless relative specifiers, so the published ESM build and its .d.ts files fail for ESM consumers. Adding the extensions in the TypeScript source breaks the ts-jest test runner's module resolution, so the safe fix is a post-build rewrite of the already-emitted ESM output only, leaving source and the CJS tree untouched.
changes: In postbuild.mjs, after the format markers are written, walk dist/esm recursively and rewrite relative specifiers (./x, ../x) lacking an extension in every .js and .d.ts file to end in .js; when a specifier resolves to a directory containing index.js, map it to <spec>/index.js, decided by inspecting the emitted dist/esm filesystem.

Handle static import ... from, export ... from, export * from, export { x } from, and dynamic import('...'); skip bare-package specifiers (undici, @opentelemetry/api, node:module) and specifiers that already carry an extension; do not touch string literals that are not in a real import/export position.
Make the rewrite idempotent (running postbuild twice yields byte-identical output - never .js.js).
Harden the existing checkTree verifier to scan .js AND .d.ts and exit non-zero (failing npm run build) if any extensionless relative specifier remains in dist/esm.

Add "prepublishOnly": "npm run build && npm test" to package.json scripts as a single added line, leaving all other scripts unchanged; dist/cjs output must be byte-identical to a build without the rewrite pass.
inputs: scripts/postbuild.mjs current tree-walk and verification logic
discovery: prefer a postbuild.mjs rewrite over source-level .js extensions (ts-jest resolution); dist/esm is flat
review 'Fix:' prescription for blocker 2 (extensionless ESM specifiers) plus the missing-prepublishOnly should-fix
phases.expectedResult: scripts/postbuild.mjs rewrites all dist/esm .js and .d.ts relative specifiers to .js idempotently, the verifier fails the build if any extensionless relative specifier remains, dist/cjs is untouched, and package.json has a prepublishOnly running build + test.
phases.compensation: Remove the rewrite pass from postbuild.mjs and the prepublishOnly line; dist is regenerated on every build, so nothing persists.

rubric.label: Every relative specifier in emitted ESM ends in .js
rubric.ruleStatement: After npm run build, no relative import/export specifier in any .js or .d.ts file under dist/esm is extensionless; the rewrite covers static import ... from, export ... from, export * from, export { x } from, and dynamic import('...'), at any nesting depth. 10 = a nodenext typecheck of dist/esm/index.d.ts passes and a real import() of dist/esm/index.js resolves every hop; 8 = grep finds no extensionless relative specifier in .js or .d.ts; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: npm run build in packages/elenwatch, then a grep for relative from/import( specifiers in dist/esm *.js and *.d.ts that lack a .js/.json/.node extension - output is empty.
grep the ESM tree for export * from './ and export { ... } from './ and confirm every such line ends .js'.
grep the ESM tree for import('./ / import("../ and confirm every relative dynamic-import literal ends in .js.
node --input-type=module -e "import('./dist/esm/index.js').then(()=>process.exit(0),e=>{console.error(e);process.exit(1)})" exits 0.
A nodenext typecheck of the emitted dist/esm/*.d.ts reports no TS2307 / extensionless-resolution errors.
failureExamples: The rewrite matches from './x' in import/export but misses export * from './options' (no braces), so a nodenext consumer gets TS2307.
Dynamic import('./worker') inside a function body is left untouched because the rewrite only scanned lines beginning with import/export.
Only .js files are walked; .d.ts files keep from './interceptor' and a strict nodenext typecheck of the published types fails.

rubric.label: Bare, already-extensioned, and non-specifier strings are untouched
rubric.ruleStatement: The rewrite changes only relative module specifiers that lack a resolvable extension; it never alters bare-package specifiers, specifiers already ending in an extension, or string literals that merely resemble a path inside ordinary code/data. 10 = a diff of dist/esm with vs without the pass shows only import/export/import() specifier lines changed; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: grep for from 'undici' / @opentelemetry/api / node:module in dist/esm shows those specifiers unchanged.
A diff of dist/esm built with vs without the rewrite: every changed line is an import/export/import() specifier, zero changes inside string literals, comments, or template contents.
No specifier in dist/esm ends in .js.js, .json.js, or .node.js.
A source string literal used as data (not an import) is byte-identical in dist/esm output.
node -e "require('./dist/cjs/index.js')" and the ESM load both still resolve the optional-peers path unchanged.
failureExamples: A broad regex rewrites a plain string literal const rel = './x' to './x.js', corrupting runtime logic that used it as a key.
The pattern appends .js to import x from 'undici' because it keyed on the import keyword rather than a leading ./ or ../.
A specifier already written as './version.js' gets a second .js -> './version.js.js'.

rubric.label: Directory targets map to /index.js, file targets to .js
rubric.ruleStatement: When a relative specifier resolves to a directory in dist/esm (a folder containing index.js), the rewrite produces <spec>/index.js; when it resolves to a sibling file, it produces <spec>.js. The choice is made by inspecting the emitted filesystem, not by guessing. 10 = explicit code + a unit test for the directory case even though dist/esm is currently flat; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: For a specifier targeting a sibling file, it was rewritten to <name>.js and that file exists on disk.
Runtime load (node --input-type=module -e "import('./dist/esm/index.js')") exits 0, proving no specifier points at a non-existent path.
Spot-check that each referenced <path>.js file actually exists in dist/esm.
Since dist/esm currently has no nested directories, the phase still contains explicit code (and ideally a fixture test) handling the directory -> /index.js case with a comment or test asserting it.
failureExamples: The rewrite unconditionally appends .js, so a future export * from './submodule' (a folder) becomes './submodule.js' which does not exist and the ESM build throws ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on load.
The existence check is run against the src tree instead of dist/esm, giving wrong answers when emit layout differs.

rubric.label: Rewrite is idempotent and the verifier now fails the build
rubric.ruleStatement: Running the postbuild step twice over the same dist/esm yields byte-identical output, and the postbuild ESM verification exits non-zero (failing npm run build) if any extensionless relative specifier remains in dist/esm (.js or .d.ts). 10 = a hash comparison of a double-run plus a demonstrated red build on a reintroduced bad specifier; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: Build, hash dist/esm, run node scripts/postbuild.mjs again, re-hash - the two hashes are identical.
Temporarily reintroduce from './interceptor' (no extension) into a built file, run the verify step, and confirm it exits non-zero naming the offending file/specifier.
The verifier check is wired into the path npm run build runs (reintroducing the bad specifier and running npm run build fails).
The verifier scans .d.ts as well as .js and distinguishes relative from bare specifiers (a bare undici import does not trip it).
npm run build on the clean tree exits 0 and the verifier reports success.
failureExamples: The rewrite appends .js on every run, so a second postbuild turns ./interceptor.js into ./interceptor.js.js.
The verifier only console.warns on a remaining extensionless specifier and still process.exit(0).
The verifier regex also flags legitimate from 'undici', making every build fail.

rubric.label: CJS tree untouched and prepublishOnly gate added
rubric.ruleStatement: The postbuild rewrite touches only dist/esm; dist/cjs output is byte-identical to a build without the rewrite pass. package.json gains exactly "prepublishOnly": "npm run build && npm test" in scripts and nothing else changes. 10 = diff -r of dist/cjs with vs without the pass is identical and package.json diff is a single added line; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: Build with the rewrite pass, then with it disabled, and diff -r the two dist/cjs trees - identical.
grep for require('./...js') in dist/cjs shows CJS require calls were not given or stripped extensions by this phase.
node -e "const m=require('./packages/elenwatch/dist/cjs/index.js'); process.exit(typeof m.Interceptor==='function'?0:1)" exits 0.
npm pkg get scripts.prepublishOnly returns exactly "npm run build && npm test"; package.json diff shows a single added line, no other script reordered.
failureExamples: The tree-walk starts at dist/ instead of dist/esm/, so require('./interceptor') in dist/cjs gets needlessly rewritten.
prepublishOnly is added as the deprecated "prepublish" hook, or as "npm test" omitting the build.
The rewrite mutates .d.ts files shared between dist/cjs and dist/esm, indirectly changing the CJS types.

phases.healerHint: Key the rewrite strictly on ./ and ../ specifiers in real import/export/dynamic-import positions, resolve each against the actual dist/esm filesystem (file -> .js, directory -> /index.js), skip anything already extensioned or bare, make it a no-op on a second run, harden the verifier to exit non-zero across .js and .d.ts, and touch package.json only for the single prepublishOnly line.

phases.name: Add pack-and-import smoke test for the published tarball
phases.goal: Add a test that runs npm pack, installs the resulting tarball into a fresh temp directory, then loads it both as an ESM import() and a CJS require() in separate node child processes, failing on any ESM regression from the createRequire or specifier-rewrite phases and skipping cleanly when npm is unavailable.
phases.rationale: The existing build tests inspect files in the workspace, not the artifact users actually download. A test that packs the tarball, installs it into a clean directory, and loads it both ways is the only check that would catch a broken ESM specifier or a require-in-ESM failure before publish.
changes: Follow the src/packaging-build.test.ts pattern: run npm pack into a temp dir, capture the produced .tgz, then npm install <tarball> into a fresh mkdtemp package.

Spawn a node child with --input-type=module doing import('elenwatch') that routes any rejection to process.exit(1) and otherwise exits 0 only if typeof m.Interceptor === 'function' && typeof m.VERSION === 'string'; assert the child exit code is 0 and surface its stderr on failure.
Spawn a separate CJS node child running require('elenwatch') asserting Interceptor is a constructor and VERSION is a string; assert exit 0.
Every pack/install/child call gets an explicit timeout and the child spawns cap maxBuffer; give the test a finite per-test timeout generous enough for npm install (>= 60s).

Probe npm availability (npm --version) and on failure call test.skip / describe.skip (not return) so the runner reports skipped, mirroring the undici-peer skip idiom; clean every temp dir and the .tgz in afterAll even on failure; name the file *.smoke.test.ts so npm test collects it.
inputs: src/packaging-build.test.ts existing pack/install pattern
success criterion 3 (smoke test runs in the verify gate and fails on ESM regressions)
outputs of the createRequire and specifier-rewrite phases (what the test must exercise)
phases.expectedResult: A new *.smoke.test.ts that packs, installs the real tarball into a temp dir, and loads elenwatch as both ESM and CJS in separate node children - green after phases 1 and 2, red if either regresses, skipped when npm is unavailable, with temp dirs cleaned up.
phases.compensation: Delete the test file; no runtime or packaging effect.

rubric.label: Loads from the packed, freshly-installed tarball
rubric.ruleStatement: The smoke test must resolve elenwatch from a tarball produced by npm pack and installed into a fresh temporary directory with no other link to the workspace, never from the workspace/src/dist path. 10 = a deliberately broken ESM specifier makes the test go red and restoring makes it green; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: The test invokes npm pack (not just --dry-run) and captures the produced .tgz filename.
It runs npm install <tarball> into a dir created via fs.mkdtemp / os.tmpdir() that is not inside the package directory.

Every child's import/require target is the bare specifier 'elenwatch', resolved with cwd pointing at the temp install - no relative path, dist, src, or require.resolve of the workspace in the child code.
Removing a .js extension from a dist/esm specifier and rebuilding+running turns the test RED; restoring turns it GREEN.
failureExamples: Test does import('../dist/esm/index.js') directly, so it passes even with extensionless ESM specifiers.
Test runs npm pack --dry-run and only asserts on the printed file list without importing anything.
Test installs the directory (npm install /path/to/packages/elenwatch) instead of the .tgz.

rubric.label: Exercises both ESM import and CJS require in separate node processes
rubric.ruleStatement: The test loads the installed package in two distinct node child processes - one native ESM import('elenwatch'), one CJS require('elenwatch') - and asserts each exits 0 with a real check on the loaded module object. 10 = reverting phase 2 makes only the ESM child fail and the test fails with that child's stderr; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: Two separate spawnSync/execFile invocations of node exist: one with --input-type=module (or a .mjs file) doing import('elenwatch'), one CJS doing require('elenwatch').
Each child asserts typeof m.Interceptor === 'function' AND typeof m.VERSION === 'string' and maps the result to its exit code.
The parent asserts status === 0 for BOTH children and fails with the child's stderr in the message.
Reverting phase 2 (bare require) leaves the CJS child passing but the ESM child exits non-zero and the test fails.
Neither child shares a process with the other or with the test runner.
failureExamples: Test only spawns the ESM child and assumes CJS 'obviously works'.
Test does const m = await import('elenwatch') inside the test itself (runner's own resolver), not a child node.
Both checks collapsed to if (m.Interceptor) truthy, so VERSION being undefined still passes.

rubric.label: ESM child's import rejection propagates to a non-zero exit
rubric.ruleStatement: A rejected dynamic import() or a thrown load error in either child must deterministically produce a non-zero exit code - not caught, defaulted, or racing process exit. 10 = an injected syntax break in dist/esm makes the ESM child exit non-zero with the module error on stderr; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: The ESM child has no bare .catch(() => {}) / .catch(() => process.exit(0)); any .catch calls process.exit(1) (or rethrows) and logs to stderr.
The child uses process.exit(cond ? 0 : 1) inside .then, or top-level await, so it cannot exit 0 before the import settles.
Injecting a syntax-breaking edit into a dist/esm file and running makes the ESM child exit non-zero, stderr contains the module error, the test fails.
The parent does not treat a spawn timeout or a null status as a pass.
failureExamples: Child is import('elenwatch').then(...).catch(() => process.exit(0)) - a broken build exits 0.
Child does import('elenwatch'); process.exit(0) without awaiting.
Parent checks status !== 1 specifically, so a segfault/timeout (status null) reads as acceptable.

rubric.label: Skips (not fails) cleanly when npm/network is unavailable
rubric.ruleStatement: When npm cannot be invoked or the pack/install step fails for environmental reasons, the suite must skip in a way the runner reports as skipped, never as a failure or a false pass, mirroring the undici-peer skip idiom. 10 = running with npm shadowed by a failing stub reports the suite skipped and the overall run exit code stays 0; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: The test probes npm availability and on failure calls test.skip / describe.skip / this.skip(), not return out of the test body.
Running with PATH stripped of npm reports the suite as skipped, the overall run exit code is 0, no assertion fires.
The skip guard wraps the pack AND the install (a mid-way install failure is classified as skip or clearly distinguished from a genuine load regression).
The skip path matches the shape of the existing undici-peer skip idiom.
failureExamples: On npm failure the test does console.warn('skipping'); return; - counted as a passed test, so CI stays green though the smoke test never ran.
npm-missing throws from spawnSync and propagates, turning an environment gap into a red build.
Only npm pack is guarded; a later offline npm install throws unhandled.

rubric.label: Cleans up temp dirs and bounds every spawned step
rubric.ruleStatement: All temp directories and tarballs the test creates must be removed in teardown even on failure, and every pack/install/child call must have an explicit timeout so a hang fails fast. 10 = after a forced-failure run no elenwatch-* dirs remain under os.tmpdir() and no stray .tgz; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: afterAll does fs.rm(tmpDir, { recursive: true, force: true }) for every temp path and removes the .tgz; cleanup is not inside the test body.
After a full run (including a forced-failure run) no elenwatch-* dirs remain under os.tmpdir() and no stray .tgz in the package dir.
Each spawnSync/execFileSync for pack, install, and both children passes an explicit timeout; child spawns cap maxBuffer.
The per-test timeout is finite and >= 60s (not the 5s default, not 0/disabled).
Pack runs once per file (beforeAll), reused by both children.
failureExamples: afterAll only runs on success paths / is missing, so every CI run leaks a node_modules tree under /tmp.
Children spawned with no timeout; a deadlock hangs the job until the CI-level kill.
Per-test timeout left at the runner default, so an 8s npm install flakes red.

rubric.label: Runs as part of the build/verify gate
rubric.ruleStatement: The smoke test must execute under the standard npm test that the release gate runs, with a filename the runner picks up, so success criterion 3 holds without an extra opt-in step. 10 = running the plain project test command lists the suite and the two children execute with npm present; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: The file matches the jest testRegex (*.test.ts / *.smoke.test.ts) - confirm by running the plain test command and seeing the suite listed.
npm test (and prepublishOnly, which chains npm test) invokes this suite with no separate script, tag, or env flag.
In an environment with npm present, the two children actually execute (verified locally).
The test does not depend on a pre-existing dist without the gate's build step running first (pretest builds).
failureExamples: File named pack-and-import.smoke.ts (no .test.), so the runner never collects it.
Suite is describe.skip by default with a comment 'enable manually before release'.
Test reads dist/esm but nothing guarantees a build ran first.

phases.healerHint: The test must npm pack then npm install the real .tgz into a fresh mkdtemp dir and load the bare 'elenwatch' specifier in two separate node children (one --input-type=module import(), one CJS require()), each asserting exit 0 with Interceptor a function and VERSION a string, with the ESM rejection routed to process.exit(1) (never swallowed), explicit per-step timeouts, test.skip when npm is absent, afterAll temp cleanup, and a filename the default npm test run collects.

phases.name: Quiet the cap-trip warning for callback users
phases.goal: In appendChunk's cap-trip path, emit the body-dropped console.error warning only when no onBodyDropped callback was configured, so applications that handle the event structurally do not also get unconditional stderr noise.
phases.rationale: When a request or response body exceeds the size cap, the library both fires the caller's optional onBodyDropped callback and writes a line to stderr. A caller who supplied the callback has explicitly taken ownership of that signal, so the extra stderr write is just noise in their logs. appendChunk is the helper that accumulates body chunks and trips the cap; it has a single console.error site shared by both directions.
changes: At the cap-trip branch (interceptor.ts ~line 623), wrap the console.error(...) call in if (capCtx.onDropped === undefined).
Leave capCtx.onDropped?.(info) and the bodyDropped flip unconditional and in place.

Add tests with a jest.spyOn(console, 'error') that is restored in afterEach: cap trips with a callback -> callback fired once, console.error spy not called; cap trips without a callback -> console.error spy called (matching the expected message).
inputs: interceptor.ts appendChunk cap-trip path (~lines 610-635, single console.error at 623)
review should-fix: unconditional cap-trip console.error
onBodyDropped / BodyDroppedInfo contract in src/options.ts
phases.expectedResult: A passing test showing the cap-trip console.error is suppressed when onBodyDropped is set (with the callback still fired) and still emitted when it is not, for both request and response directions.
phases.compensation: Remove the if guard to restore the unconditional console.error; no external effect.

rubric.label: Console.error fires only when no callback is configured
rubric.ruleStatement: In appendChunk's cap-trip branch, the body-dropped console.error is emitted if and only if capCtx.onDropped is undefined; supplying onBodyDropped fully silences that stderr line. 10 = the message text/level is unchanged for the no-callback case and zero stderr for the callback case, both asserted with a spy; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: The cap-trip console.error(...) call is wrapped in a condition equivalent to capCtx.onDropped === undefined (or !capCtx.onDropped), not the negation.
Runtime: an Interceptor with a small maxBodyBytes and an onBodyDropped callback, over-cap body -> zero console.error / stderr writes from the cap-trip path.
Runtime: same scenario with onBodyDropped omitted -> exactly the same stderr line as before this phase (message and level unchanged).
grep shows no cap-trip console.error call left outside the guard.

Guard added but the message is downgraded to console.warn or reworded.

rubric.label: onBodyDropped(info) still invoked unconditionally
rubric.ruleStatement: The structured onDropped(info) call fires exactly as before - once per direction when the byte counter first exceeds the cap - and the bodyDropped flip is unchanged, regardless of the new logging guard. 10 = git diff shows the callback and flip untouched and outside the guard; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: onDropped(info) sits outside and independent of the if (capCtx.onDropped === undefined) block.
With a callback set and an over-cap body, the callback receives one BodyDroppedInfo with the same fields as before.
The bodyDropped flag is still flipped in the same place under the same condition.
git diff shows no change to the fire-once logic (the callback is not moved into an else branch).

The whole cap-trip block (flag flip + callback + log) is wrapped in the guard, so callers with a callback never get bodyDropped set.

rubric.label: Guard covers request and response directions
rubric.ruleStatement: Every cap-trip console.error site - for both request-body and response-body accumulators - is behind the callback-absence guard, with no unconditional stderr write remaining in either path. 10 = grep confirms exactly one guarded console.error and a runtime check for the response direction; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: grep -n "console.error" over interceptor.ts cross-referenced with the cap-trip region shows every body-dropped log site guarded.
Since request and response share the single appendChunk helper, confirm there is only one log site and it is guarded.
Runtime: an over-cap RESPONSE body with onBodyDropped set produces no cap-trip stderr line.
Runtime: an over-cap REQUEST body with onBodyDropped set produces no cap-trip stderr line.
failureExamples: A second, direction-specific console.error elsewhere in the response-drain branch is left unconditional.
Only the request path is exercised in tests, leaving a response-direction regression uncaught.

rubric.label: Tests assert both states via a console.error spy
rubric.ruleStatement: interceptor.test.ts adds tests that spy on console.error and assert both the callback-set outcome (spy not called, callback called) and the callback-unset outcome (spy called), with the spy restored. 10 = both directions and both states covered with a guaranteed mockRestore; minScore = acceptable.

A separate assertion triggers a cap trip with onBodyDropped unset and asserts the console.error spy was called (ideally matching the message).
The spy is jest.spyOn(console, 'error') and restored in afterEach/finally via mockRestore.
npm test passes and npm run lint exits 0; the new tests pass in isolation and as part of the full file.
failureExamples: jest.spyOn(console, 'error') is never restored, so a later suite sees a permanent mock.

rubric.label: Change is limited to the logging guard
rubric.ruleStatement: The diff touches only the cap-trip logging guard and its tests - no change to BodyDroppedInfo shape, cap threshold math, maxBodyBytes defaults, the wire/capture split, or any public option. 10 = mentally reverting the single guard restores today's behavior with nothing dangling; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: git diff is confined to the cap-trip branch of interceptor.ts (~lines 610-635) plus interceptor.test.ts.
No edits to src/options.ts, the onBodyDropped type, or the fire-once counter comparison.
The compensation is exactly 'remove the if guard'.
No new public option or config field introduced.

phases.healerHint: Wrap only the cap-trip console.error in if (capCtx.onDropped === undefined) at the single shared log site, leave onDropped(info) and the bodyDropped flip unconditional, and add console.error-spy tests for both states and both directions with a guaranteed mockRestore.

phases.name: Write full README Installation, Configuration, Limitations, API sections
phases.goal: Replace the 31-line packages/elenwatch/README.md with complete Installation, Configuration, Limitations, and API sections that document the real post-fix behavior of the package.
phases.rationale: The current package README is too thin to publish and this horizon's own definition of done requires it. Users need to know that payload capture defaults to off, that redaction matches its needles as case-insensitive substrings and can over-redact, how the body-size cap and its callback behave (including that the stderr fallback is silenced when a callback is supplied), that global fetch capture requires the optional undici peer, that requestTransform only sees the HTTP path, that streamed request bodies are buffered rather than truly streamed (though delivered to the wire in full), and that only one interceptor can run per process.
changes: Installation: npm install elenwatch, plus that undici is an OPTIONAL peer required only for global fetch capture (silently skipped if absent) and the OpenTelemetry packages are optional peers required only for otelSpanLogger.

Configuration: capturePayloads (default false, no bodies emitted); maxBodyBytes (default 10 MiB = 10*1024*1024 bytes, applied independently per direction) and onBodyDropped (BodyDroppedInfo = {host, direction, bytes, cap}; fires at most once per (host,direction); the stderr fallback is silenced when the callback is set); redaction with an explicit warning that needles match as case-insensitive SUBSTRINGS of field names and can over-redact unrelated fields (e.g. any key containing 'address'). Include a copy-pasteable options reference.

Limitations: requestTransform is applied only on the HTTP/HTTPS path and NOT to global fetch request bodies (which are captured but never transformed), asymmetric with responseTransform; streamed request bodies are fully buffered before dispatch (not truly streamed) though delivered to the server byte-for-byte even over maxBodyBytes; only one interceptor can be active per process, and install() patches http.ClientRequest.prototype and the global undici dispatcher.

API: the Interceptor class with .install() / .restore(), the Logger type, otelSpanLogger, VERSION, and InterceptorOptions fields - matching the actual named exports in src/index.ts (no default export, no free install/restore functions); every import { ... } from 'elenwatch' line uses only real exports; at least one complete runnable example.
inputs: src/options.ts docstrings and src/index.ts exports (canonical wording and API surface)
final behavior from the split-wire-body and console-error-gating phases (streamed-body caveat; stderr silenced when a callback is set)
the undici optional-peer caveat established by the createRequire phase
success criterion 7 topic list
phases.expectedResult: packages/elenwatch/README.md with populated Installation, Configuration, Limitations, and API sections covering all seven documentation points in success criterion 7, with every code snippet valid and every documented symbol a real export.
phases.compensation: Restore the previous README.md from git; documentation-only, no code effect.

rubric.label: All four required sections present and populated
rubric.ruleStatement: README.md must contain non-empty Installation, Configuration, Limitations, and API sections a reader can locate by heading. 10 = each section is substantive prose plus a table or runnable code block, logically ordered, README >= 120 lines with no TODO/TBD markers; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: README.md has a Markdown heading matching each of Installation, Configuration, Limitations, API (case-insensitive, any level).
Each of the four sections has at least 3 lines of substantive prose or a table/code block below its heading - not a placeholder.
README.md is materially longer than the prior 31-line stub (>= 120 lines) and contains no 'TODO', 'TBD', or 'coming soon'.
Section ordering is logical (Installation before Configuration before API); Limitations is a top-level section.
failureExamples: Limitations content exists only as two sentences appended to Configuration with no heading.
A README thorough on Installation/Configuration/API but silently omitting Limitations.
API contains only 'See source for details.'

rubric.label: Configuration section matches canonical option semantics
rubric.ruleStatement: Every option documented must state behavior and defaults matching src/options.ts, with the capture/cap/redaction topics all covered. 10 = a copy-pasteable options table with exact types and defaults plus the redaction over-redaction example; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: capturePayloads documented as defaulting to false, with the consequence that no request/response body is emitted by default.
maxBodyBytes documented with default exactly '10 MiB (10 * 1024 * 1024 bytes)' AND stated to apply independently per direction.

onBodyDropped documented as firing at most once per (host, direction), with the BodyDroppedInfo shape giving all four fields: host (string), direction ('request' | 'response'), bytes (number), cap (number).
The doc states the stderr/console.error warning is emitted only when no onBodyDropped callback is configured and is silenced when a callback is supplied.

Redaction documented as matching needles as case-insensitive SUBSTRINGS of field names (not exact names), with an explicit over-redaction warning and a concrete example such as a key containing 'address'.
A copy-pasteable options reference lists each InterceptorOptions field with its type and default.
failureExamples: Doc states 'redaction masks fields whose names exactly match the sensitive-field list' - wrong; it is case-insensitive substring.
Doc gives maxBodyBytes default as '1 MiB' or omits that the cap is per-direction.
Doc describes onBodyDropped but never mentions that setting it suppresses the stderr line.
BodyDroppedInfo documented as {host, direction, size} - 'size' is wrong (it is 'bytes') and 'cap' is missing.

rubric.label: Limitations section covers the three known constraints correctly
rubric.ruleStatement: The Limitations section must accurately describe the requestTransform HTTP-path asymmetry, the buffered-not-streamed-but-delivered-in-full request body behavior, and the one-interceptor-per-process model. 10 = each stated precisely with no contradiction elsewhere in the README; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: States requestTransform is applied only on the HTTP/HTTPS path and NOT to global fetch request bodies (captured/logged but never transformed); notes this is asymmetric with responseTransform.

States streamed request bodies are fully buffered in memory before dispatch (not truly streamed), AND explicitly states the full body is still delivered to the server byte-for-byte even when it exceeds maxBodyBytes (only the logged copy truncates).
States only one interceptor can be active per process, and that install() patches http.ClientRequest.prototype and the global undici dispatcher.
No limitation is contradicted elsewhere in the README.
failureExamples: Doc claims 'requestTransform runs for both the http module and global fetch' - wrong.
Doc says a request body larger than maxBodyBytes is 'truncated before being sent', implying wire corruption - wrong after the split-wire-body phase.
Limitations omits the one-interceptor-per-process constraint.

rubric.label: Installation documents optional peers accurately
rubric.ruleStatement: The Installation section must describe undici and the OpenTelemetry packages as optional peer dependencies with the correct consequence of their absence. 10 = the silent-skip consequence is stated for each; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: Shows the base install command npm install elenwatch.
States undici is an OPTIONAL peer required only for global fetch capture, and that fetch capture is silently skipped (no error) when undici is absent.
States the OpenTelemetry packages (e.g. @opentelemetry/api) are optional peers required only for otelSpanLogger.
Does not list undici or the OTEL packages as mandatory dependencies.
failureExamples: Doc says 'elenwatch requires undici' or puts undici in a required-prerequisites list.
Installation mentions only npm install elenwatch and never mentions the undici peer, so a reader cannot explain why fetch calls are not captured.

rubric.label: API section and code snippets match the real export surface
rubric.ruleStatement: Every symbol, import, and code example in the README must correspond to an actual export from src/index.ts and the real Interceptor API. 10 = at least one complete runnable example and zero references to non-existent symbols; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: API section documents the Interceptor class with instance methods .install() and .restore() - NOT standalone install()/restore() functions.
Documents the Logger type, otelSpanLogger, and VERSION as exports; any other documented symbol actually appears in src/index.ts.
Every import { ... } from 'elenwatch' line imports only names exported by src/index.ts.
At least one complete, runnable usage example: construct new Interceptor({...}), call .install(), reference .restore() for teardown.
No example imports a default export or a free install / restore function.
failureExamples: README shows import { install } from 'elenwatch'; install() - no such export.
API doc lists startInterceptor() / stopInterceptor() helpers that do not exist.
Example does import elenwatch from 'elenwatch' (default import) - index.ts has only named exports.

rubric.label: Code snippets are syntactically valid and self-consistent
rubric.ruleStatement: All fenced code blocks must be valid for their declared language and consistent with the option semantics documented elsewhere in the README. 10 = every block is language-tagged and parses, and option values respect documented types; minScore = acceptable.
passCriteria: Every fenced block has a language tag; TS/JS blocks parse without syntax errors.
Option values shown respect documented types (maxBodyBytes is a number of bytes, onBodyDropped is a function taking one BodyDroppedInfo arg).
An onBodyDropped example uses the parameter fields exactly as named in BodyDroppedInfo (host, direction, bytes, cap).
Shell blocks use real commands; no invented CLI (elenwatch has no binary).
failureExamples: An example passes maxBodyBytes: '10mb' (string).
onBodyDropped example logs info.reason or info.field - fields that do not exist.
A code block tagged ```ts contains prose or an unterminated template literal.

phases.healerHint: Ground every claim in src/options.ts docstrings and src/index.ts: correct any wrong defaults (maxBodyBytes = 10 MiB, per-direction; capturePayloads = false), restate redaction as case-insensitive substring matching with an over-redaction warning, replace any free install()/restore() usage with new Interceptor(...).install()/.restore(), add the undici-optional-peer caveat to Installation, and ensure Limitations spells out the requestTransform-is-HTTP-path-only asymmetry plus buffered-but-delivered-in-full streamed request bodies.

successCriteria: A streamed fetch request body larger than maxBodyBytes is delivered to the wire in full and byte-identical while only the capture-side buffer is truncated (blocker 1 resolved), proven by a 5000-byte body / 1024-byte cap regression test with a server-side assertion.
